Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on the hands, primarily the palms; dryness in other areas (legs) but less severe; itching of palms; occasional bleeding with scratching.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptom onset about 3–4 months ago; gradually worsening; now painful and affecting ability to work.
- History of presenting illness details: Works as a hotel housekeeper; gloves not consistently worn; recently changed job ~4 months ago; likely exposure to cleaning products.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Non-smoker; alcohol use: a couple of pints per week; occupation as hotel housekeeper with variable glove use.
- Family history: Diabetes noted; no specific skin condition family history documented.

Objective:
- No explicit vitals or physical examination findings documented in transcript.
- Symptoms described by patient include palm involvement with dryness, cracking, itching, and occasional scratching-related bleeding.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dermatitis (likely contact dermatitis)
   - Assessment: Dermatitis / probable contact dermatitis from occupational exposure (cleaning products) with palm-dalm involvement and skin cracking.
   - Differential diagnoses: Irritant contact dermatitis; allergic contact dermatitis.
   - Investigations: None planned at this time.
   - Treatment:
     - Avoid triggers: wear gloves at all times during cleaning.
     - Topical corticosteroid cream to reduce inflammation (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Emollients/strong moisturizers: apply 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
     - Follow-up: return in 10–14 days if not improved; sooner if symptoms worsen or spreading.
     - Prescription: Will send a prescription to the patient’s pharmacy.
   - Referrals: None.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
   - Assessment: Known type 2 diabetes mellitus.
   - Differential diagnoses: None specified.
   - Investigations: None planned.
